acceptance_test.text: Add a test that (a) calls native_codex_provider_response_schema() first, then (b) calls load_native_codex_schema() and asserts 'finding_dispositions' is still absent from schema["$defs"]["plan_result"]["required"], and (c) successfully re-parses a historical plan_result document lacking finding_dispositions via parse_bound_native_codex_contract_result() after step (a). If this ordering fails, native_codex_provider_response_schema() must deep-copy the schema (e.g. copy.deepcopy or a JSON round-trip) before mutating 'required' so any cached/shared schema used to validate persisted documents is never affected by a provider-schema request.

new_findings.summary: native_codex_contract.py's native_codex_provider_response_schema() does `schema = load_native_codex_schema()` and then mutates the returned object in place: `required = schema["$defs"]["plan_result"]["required"]; required.append("finding_dispositions")`. If load_native_codex_schema() is, or ever becomes, memoized/returns a shared dict (a very natural optimization for a schema read on every native-document validation), this in-place list mutation leaks into every later call to load_native_codex_schema(), permanently making finding_dispositions required for plan_result validation everywhere -- including validate_native_codex_document()/parse_bound_native_codex_contract_result() calls that must keep accepting already-persisted historical plan_result documents. That is exactly the guarantee C-02 exists to protect. The new regression test test_historical_plan_result_without_dispositions_remains_readable cannot catch this because it calls load_native_codex_schema() (asserting the field absent) BEFORE calling native_codex_provider_response_schema() (the only call that performs the mutation) in the same test, so any aliasing leak would go undetected by the current suite in either ordering across tests or process lifetime.

acceptance_test.text: Either remove the unused require_structured parameter from replay_findings() and document that legacy/unstructured finding-transition records are unconditionally excluded for cross-work-unit identifier safety, or implement and test a genuine require_structured=False code path before any caller (including a future Slice 2 Markdown convergence projection) relies on it to surface legacy transitions.

new_findings.summary: artifact_replay.py's replay_findings() accepts a require_structured flag, but its only use is: `if payload.work_unit_id is None: if require_structured: continue  # comment  continue` -- both branches unconditionally continue, so require_structured currently has no observable effect; unstructured/legacy finding-transition records are always excluded from the projection regardless of the flag. Every current caller (ProductionWorkflowDriver.authoritative_native_findings) passes require_structured=True, so this is not a live bug today, but the parameter and its docstring imply a real fallback mode for legacy records (plausibly needed by Slice 2's planned Markdown convergence projection) that does not actually exist, risking silent functional gaps or reviewer confusion later.

pre_mortem: If C-01/C-02 are closed wrongly here, the most likely path is that a later, unrelated performance change adds caching to load_native_codex_schema() -- a natural next step for a schema read on every native-document validation -- which silently activates the required-field mutation performed by native_codex_provider_response_schema(). Every previously-valid persisted plan_result document then fails validation on its next replay or record-ahead recovery, reintroducing precisely the incompatibility C-02 was meant to foreclose, but the failure would only surface much later when an old run is resumed, far from this review and far from the commit that introduced the caching.

review_evidence.break_condition: This disposition breaks if load_native_codex_schema() is shown to return a memoized/shared object with no defensive copy added before the 'required' mutation in native_codex_provider_response_schema() (C-03), or if any authorized-path test covering PLAN/CORRECTION mirror-divergence guards, record-ahead-precedes-guard behavior, or legacy-payload-shape preservation is found to be absent, skipped, or non-passing in the actual full-matrix run rather than passing as attested (1156 passed in 170.69s).
review_evidence.dimensions: Contract compatibility: plan_result gained an optional finding_dispositions field kept out of the persisted/validated schema's required list while the live provider-request schema enforces it (test_native_codex_contract.py). Reviewer-owned authority: FindingTransitionPayload gained optional structured opening/response fields with __post_init__ guards (opening metadata only on 'opened', response_decision only on 'responded'), and replay_findings() re-checks reporter/severity ownership per transition, preserving 'Codex may only respond, never open/close/reclassify'. Append ordering & record-ahead recovery: _bind_authoritative_native_findings is invoked only in the 'recovered is None' branch, matching the documented precedence, and is exercised by dedicated tests for both Codex request kinds and the Claude review path (test_combined_native_codex_record_ahead_recovery_precedes_mirror_guard, test_native_record_ahead_recovery_receives_full_history_and_skips_provider). Request binding: build_native_review_request now embeds persisted FindingResponse entries and the validation attestation into the request id (test_request_binds_persisted_codex_disposition_and_attestation). Legacy isolation: finding_payload() defaults to the pre-existing minimal (work_unit_id=None) payload shape unless a work_unit_id is supplied (test_finding_payload_preserves_legacy_shape_and_native_authority), and legacy Claude-review persistence is explicitly wired with structured=False. Fail-closed behavior: authoritative_native_findings raises WorkflowExecutionError on any mismatch between the replayed record chain and the state-v3 mirror, and on missing/invalid combined-native binding, before any provider invocation.
review_evidence.largest_residual_risk: native_codex_provider_response_schema() mutates the dict returned by load_native_codex_schema() in place (appending to schema["$defs"]["plan_result"]["required"]) instead of copying it first; if load_native_codex_schema() is or becomes cached/shared, this silently makes finding_dispositions required for every subsequent validation of already-persisted plan_result documents, defeating the exact backward-compatibility guarantee C-02 was closed on, and the current suite cannot detect it because the one test exercising both functions happens to call load_native_codex_schema() before native_codex_provider_response_schema().

status_changes.rationale: tests/test_workflow.py::test_combined_native_codex_finding_steps_fail_before_provider_on_mirror_drift is parametrized over WorkflowStep.CODEX_PLAN_REVISION and WorkflowStep.CODEX_CORRECTION and asserts WorkflowEngine._run_codex() raises WorkflowExecutionError with driver.codex_calls left empty for both, proving the mirror-vs-replay guard (_bind_authoritative_native_findings -> driver.authoritative_native_findings) fires before any provider start for the PLAN kind as well as the CORRECTION kind, not only for CODEX_CORRECTION/CODEX_FINAL_CORRECTION as C-01 warned. test_combined_native_claude_review_fails_before_provider_on_mirror_drift extends the same guard to native Claude reviews, and test_combined_native_codex_record_ahead_recovery_precedes_mirror_guard proves record-ahead recovery suppresses the guard/provider call as required by the plan. This satisfies the bound acceptance test: 'Tests prove mirror divergence stops CODEX_PLAN_REVISION and CODEX_CORRECTION before provider invocation.'

schemas/native-agent-codex-result-v1.schema.json adds finding_dispositions to plan_result as an optional (non-required) property, so load_native_codex_schema() keeps accepting historical documents without the field (test_historical_plan_result_without_dispositions_remains_readable asserts the field is absent from load_native_codex_schema()'s plan_result.required and that a historical document parses with findings==()). native_codex_provider_response_schema() adds the field to 'required' only on the live provider-facing schema, enforcing it for newly generated responses. test_plan_revision_requires_every_open_finding_disposition shows disposition completeness is enforced in native_codex_contract.py (NativeCodexErrorCode.FINDING_REFERENCE_INVALID) only when the bound context carries open findings -- a domain-layer, context-dependent rule, not an unconditional schema 'required' change. This satisfies the bound acceptance test: 'Historical plan results without finding_dispositions remain readable, new provider results require the field, and only bound open findings activate disposition completeness.' New finding C-03 flags a related schema-object-aliasing risk in the same function that should be closed out for durable assurance of this guarantee, but it does not falsify the tested behavior as currently exercised.
